_comment: Run template for irish-ahu: one real mixing-box AHU at an industrial facility, running 24/7 (the supply fan draws power in 99.2% of the rows that trend it). Hourly resample of the 15-minute store. The minimum outdoor air is undocumented, so min_oa_pct is CALIBRATED from the unit's own minimum-position months: with the OA damper held at its 20% minimum (Aug 2019 - Jun 2020, 4,581 hours with |RAT - OAT| >= 5 F) the mixing balance gives a median 4.1% outdoor-air fraction -- not a generic 20%. No fan signal is mapped (the unit never stops), so outdoor_air_fraction is not fan-gated. Rules that fit the design: outdoor-air fraction, the economizer high limit (Ireland rarely reaches it), leaking valves, simultaneous heating and cooling, and mechanical cooling in free-cooling weather. Left out: supply-air setpoint rules (no setpoint is trended), schedule and setback rules (the unit runs continuously), zone rules (the zones are not mapped). Normal-operation notes: economizer_high_limit warns (OA above the minimum in 21% of the hours above 65 F with the outdoor air no cooler than the return; the rule's differential changeover already excuses OAT < RAT): part of it is the COVID-19 100% period, but the damper also stays open in warm weather in 2017-2019 and 2022, so it is a plausible real finding. outdoor_air_fraction warns on 'excess OA' (above the 4.1% minimum in 42% of the cooling-weather hours, outdoor air above 70 F), and it is NOT mostly the documented COVID-19 period of 100% outdoor air (about 2020-08 to 2021-12-02, a deliberate operating choice): split with source.start / source.end, the years before it (2017-06 to 2020-02) show excess outdoor air in 53% of their cooling-weather hours (a fault on their own) against 45% during it (2020-08 to 2021-11). Cooling weather is rare in Ireland, so each period has few such hours; raise the pre-COVID excess with the site as a question, with the dates (workbook exercise air-economizer, question 7). leaking_valve reads 'ok' over the whole record since 0.93 (#42), judging each coil on its own leaving-air temperature (HCALTemp / CCALTemp) instead of the supply air: the heating coil rises more than 3 F above the mixed air with both valves shut in 11% of those hours before the documented 2022-05-01 valve replacement (warn on that period alone; concentrated in the 2020/21 COVID 100%-outdoor-air winter, when the entering air was coldest) and 0% after; the cooling coil reads 3 F below the mixed air in 8-9% of them on both sides of the date. Judged on the supply air, as before 0.93, the same hours read a 34% heating-leak signature before the replacement and 0.2% after: most of it sits downstream of the coils (DaTemp reads 2.6 F above CCALTemp in the median closed hour before the date, -0.7 F after -- fan heat or the supply sensor), so it was a lead to check, not a confirmed leak.
